newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police to look into corruption allegations.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police to look into corruption allegations.

text.p: Israeli justice officials ordered police on Sunday to probe allegations of high-level corruption which politicians have said could bring down Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.

A justice ministry official said the decision to investigate the government's ill-fated appointment of an attorney general was made at a meeting between state prosecutor Edna Arbel and police officials early on Sunday.

"The state prosecutor instructed the police to investigate allegations raised in the report on Channel One," said a justice ministry spokeswoman. She said investigators would ask the television to hand over evidence used to prepare the report.

State-owned Channel One television caused a furore last week by alleging that lawyer Roni Bar-On was appointed attorney general after promising to arrange a plea bargain for Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, on trial for corruption.
Bar-On resigned within 12 hours of taking office earlier this month under public criticism he was unfit for the job.

The television said Deri, after getting Bar-On's promise of a plea bargain that would save his political career, conditioned his party's support for the Hebron deal with the PLO on Bar-On being appointed attorney general.
The 10-member Shas party is one of the pillars of Netanyahu's government coalition.
Bar-On denied the television's allegations, as did Deri and Netanyahu.
The television has said it would cooperate with police but would not reveal its sources.

Asked on television on Saturday if the government could stay in office if the allegations proved accurate, Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said: "If the affair is in fact as it appears, at least, there is no doubt that this government has no place."
